newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia commercial orchards clear of blight-govt.
newsitem.headline: Australia commercial orchards clear of blight-govt.

text.p: Australian Primary Industries Minister John Anderson on Thursday said surveys had failed to detect fire blight in commercial orchards around Australia.
Fire blight had been found to be present on a limited number of ornamental host plants in the botanical gardens in Melbourne, Victoria, and in Adelaide, South Australia, he said in a statement.
"However, it is pleasing that surveys throughout Australia have failed to detect fire blight in commercial orchards, nurseries and urban areas," he said.
The implications of the results would be discussed with state and territory ministers and industry representatives soon, he said.
The fire blight bacteria, a major apple and pear disease, was recently found for the first time on Australian plants of the rose family in the botanical gardens in Adelaide and Melbourne.
The disease can devastate orchards, although the fruit is not affected.
The Australian apple and pear industry is worth around A$360 million a year.
